newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar zooms to 2-1/2 year high in Europe.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar zooms to 2-1/2 year high in Europe.

text.p: The dollar jumped to its highest level against the yen in 2-1/2 years on Monday, cheered by a rethink on Japan's economic recovery and a harmonious meeting of the world's major industrialised nations.
The dollar rose as investors began to liquidate long yen positions amid dampened enthusiasm for Japan's recovery.
The weekend meeting of Group of Seven (G7) nations in Washington also underpinned the U.S. currency with finance ministers and central bank chiefs expressing satisfaction with current exchange rates.

"A lot of people have been long of yen positions for some time and we're now seeing them slowly whittling their way out of them," said Alan Collins, head of technical analysis at Merita Bank in London.
The dollar rose to a high of 111.50 yen before retreating a little to 111.42 yen and 1.5266 marks by 0915 GMT. That compared with Friday's late European levels of 110.78 yen and 1.5239 marks.
European share markets, in contrast to the dollar, opened mixed to weak with all three of the major bourses -- London, Paris and Frankfurt -- a few points adrift in early business.
British government bonds were largely unchanged, unaffected by M0 monetary data, while German government bunds drifted slightly lower as the market consolidated recent gains.
Japan's economic prospects provided the major impetus for the dollar after August preliminary industrial output figures showed a higher-than-expected decline of 1.9 percent.

"Japan's economy has been seen as coming out of recession slowly and steadily but the industrial output figures were lower than expected," said Teddy Dewitt, bond strategist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull in London.

Japan's Finance Minister Wataru Kubo told the weekend G7 meeting he expected the Bank of Japan to keep an easy monetary stance for now with policy geared towards ensuring a Japanese economic recovery.

His comments, along those from Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita that the fall in long-term rates reflected a change in sentiment about Japan's economic prospects, were seen as encouragement to Japanese institutional investors to seek higher returns overseas.
Most share markets opened the week in subdued mood.
In London, while 4,000 remains in sight, a thin economic and corporate diary was seen keeping trade weak.
Key U.S. jobs data on Friday are expected to further cap activity in a busy week for U.S. economic figures and to keep interest rate concerns to the fore.
Wall Street's four point rise on Friday provided little lead to Europe, with London's FTSE index trading nearly five points down at 0915 GMT.

Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel, which is trying to negotiate a solution to its debt problems with creditor banks, asked for a temporary suspension of its shares in London, pending an announcement. It also requested its share listings in Paris and Brussels be suspended.

News that British Gas will seek a reference to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission to settle a price control dispute and that talks had been terminated on the sale of parts of its business in Scotland pushed Gas shares 3p lower to 197-1/2p in early trading.
French shares opened slightly weaker on profit-taking ahead of the expiry of September futures contracts later in the day.
The CAC-40 index was down 2.74 points at 2,104.31 at 0915 GMT.

German shares started bourse dealings a little lower as market treaded water in the absence of significant corporate news. Activity was very restricted in early trade, with the 30-share DAX index down eight points.
CURRENCIES AT 0915 GMT
The was trading at 111.42 yen and 1.5266 marks, compared with Friday's late European levels of 110.78 yen and 1.5239 marks.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0915
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 4.8 points at 3,941.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 2.74 points at 2,104.31.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 8.0 points at 2,651.04. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened slightly weaker at $380.30, compared with London's Friday close of $381.15. Silver was two cents down at $4.91.
